# Charter — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S06d 'Interaction connector standard — web, Telegram, MCP first', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 8, plan `docs/plans/slices/S06d-connector-standard.md`.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-8 PI plan and the standing delegation `01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14`.
- **Authority:** SPEC §4.5, §8 S6-α and §11 R11 make web, Telegram and MCP three instances of one class of user-interaction app; S06d builds the standard that makes the next connector cheap.
- **Objective:** one registry entry per connector kind — a typed config with a `schemars` schema, named sealed secrets, a default grant set, capabilities and `authenticate`/`parse`/`send` — behind one inbound route, one command grammar, one multicast dispatcher with a first-response close, and a tenant-admin grant matrix. Config and credentials are Postgres rows entered through the web UI; there are no per-connector environment variables.
- **Scope in:** the `channel`, `channel::command`, `channel::connectors` and `interaction` modules; migration 0038; `channel_binding`, `channel_action_grant` and `interaction_dispatch`; the seven `channels.*` actions; the `Authority::Channel` invoke path; the dispatch and close worker; and the web channel's human-role authorization.
- **Scope out:** a second approval state machine (the first-response loser is `expired`), per-connector environment variables, machine grants for the web channel, machine sign-off of eval gates, and workflow authoring by a channel.
- **Constraints:** a connector kind is code, not a CHECK; a secret field holds a name and never a value; the machine floor is computed and cannot be granted, enforced by both `channels.policy_set` and `invoke`; the dispatcher is idempotent by dispatch PK plus advisory lock; a webhook sender retries non-2xx, so business refusals must be 200 acks.
- **Retrospective status:** the standard was built and gated at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix. The project row is closed while its closure review, change control, baseline, WBS, registers, contract, Phase-G review and artefact set were never published; this pack is authored on 2026-11-28 to supply the lifecycle record, and it does not attest contemporaneous ceremonial review.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S06d the standard that makes every user-interaction connector an instance of one class: a typed `ConnectorSpec` per kind, one binding row, one inbound route, one command grammar, one multicast dispatcher, a first-response close and a tenant-admin grant matrix. This statement governs the retrospective record of the work built and gated at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix, re-read at the 2026-11-28 snapshot.
body.scope: In scope are `crates/actions/src/channel/{mod,command}.rs`, `crates/actions/src/channel/connectors/{mod,telegram,webhook}.rs`, `crates/actions/src/control/channels.rs`, the `Authority::Channel` and `machine_forbidden` rules in `invoke` and `spec`, the store modules for interaction, RBAC, channel and delivery, the single inbound route in `crates/api/src/routes/channels.rs`, and the dispatch and close worker in `apps/server/src/worker.rs`. Out of scope are per-connector environment variables, a second state machine, and any machine grant for the web channel.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective statement; the delivery team (conveyor-e2e) is accountable for the tree and its suites; the Architecture Board reviews the artefact set; the SRO accepts the project's closure at the tranche-8 review. Tenant admins are consulted because they own the stored grant matrix, and connector builders are the consumers the standard has to make cheap.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is the slice plan's §5 result at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix: clippy and fmt clean, the served OpenAPI lock OK, and every affected binary re-run green (`conveyor-api --lib`, `externals_declared`, `kata_role`, `channel_inbound`, `channel_policy`, `conveyor-server --test prune`, `interaction_dispatch`, `conveyor-store --lib`). The full workspace suite was not repeated end-to-end after the fixes, and that is recorded as a limitation rather than a pass.
body.constraints: Config and credentials are rows, not environment: `channels.bind` validates a binding's config against the kind's own schema and refuses a secret name the tenant does not hold. The machine floor is computed from declared scopes and resource, and both `channels.policy_set` and `invoke` enforce it, so no stored grant can widen it. Eval gates are human-only: the shared decision writer refuses a non-human or non-`evals:approve` decision on any approval with `eval_id IS NOT NULL`, and the dispatcher never offers such a gate to a machine channel.
body.retrospective: This statement is authored on 2026-11-28 for the tranche-8 rework. No contemporaneous statement of architecture work exists; the delivery was recorded in the slice plan and its gate result. The statement records what the tree, the migration and the suites prove today, and it names the one gate limitation — the full workspace suite was not repeated end to end — instead of implying it ran.

documents.title: User Stories — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# User Stories — S06d Interaction Connector Standard

## Personas

The standard serves four personas named in the slice plan's objective and its §2 table: the tenant admin, who binds a connector and owns the grant matrix; the connector builder, who adds a kind; the approval responder, who answers a gate from whichever channel they hold; and the platform operator, who runs the dispatch and close worker. The mcp kind adds the licence principal S06b supplies, so an agent can answer a gate as a machine binding without a new persona.

## Stories

- As a tenant admin, I want to bind a connector kind from the web UI with a typed config and named secrets, so that credentials are Postgres rows and no per-connector environment variable exists.
- As a connector builder, I want to add a kind as one ConnectorSpec with authenticate/parse/send, so that the next interaction app costs one registry entry rather than a subsystem.
- As an approval responder, I want a pending approval offered on every eligible channel, so that the first terminal response decides it.
- As a security owner, I want the machine floor and eval gates enforced by the action layer, so that no stored grant can widen them.
- As a platform operator, I want the losing deliveries expired and notified once, so that the decision has an auditable loss without a second state machine.

## Scenarios

Given a tenant holds a binding whose config omits a required field, when channels.bind validates it against the kind's config_schema, then the bind is refused and no row is written. Given an inbound platform payload, when the adapter authenticates with the binding's sealed secret and parses it, then the shared command grammar maps it to approve, run, close, do or help and invoke runs with Authority::Channel. Given a pending approval with two eligible machine bindings and one web inbox, when interaction.dispatch fans it out, then each gets one delivery and the dispatch primary key prevents a second fan-out. Given the first terminal decision arrives, when interaction.close runs, then every live sibling becomes expired with last_error 'superseded: resolved via <channel>' and one closure notice is sent per dispatch. Given a tenant admin tries to grant a machine channel an eval sign-off, when channels.policy_set and invoke evaluate machine_forbidden, then the grant and the call are refused.

## Verify

The stories are verified by `crates/api/tests/channel_inbound.rs` for the inbound route and grammar, `crates/api/tests/channel_policy.rs` for binding validation and the machine floor, `apps/server/tests/interaction_dispatch.rs` for multicast and the first-response close, and `crates/api/tests/externals_declared.rs` for the absence of per-connector environment configuration. The recorded verdict is the plan's §5 gate at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix, with the full workspace suite not repeated end-to-end afterwards.

documents.title: Acceptance Criteria — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Acceptance Criteria — S06d Interaction Connector Standard

## Scenarios

- AC-1 Binding validation: a config missing a required field, or naming a secret the tenant does not hold, is refused by channels.bind and no binding row is written.
- AC-2 Inbound interaction: POST /api/channels/{binding_id}/inbound resolves the binding, the adapter authenticates and parses, and invoke runs with Authority::Channel; the adapter never authorizes.
- AC-3 Shared grammar: approve, reject, answer, run, rerun, start, finish, cancel, close, create, do and help are served by one implementation for every text connector.
- AC-4 Multicast: a pending approval is offered once to every eligible machine binding and human web inbox, and the dispatch primary key makes a repeat fan-out a no-op.
- AC-5 First response: the first terminal decision expires every live sibling delivery with last_error 'superseded: resolved via <channel>' and sends one closure notice per dispatch; a delivered sibling stays delivered.
- AC-6 Machine floor: channels.policy_set cannot grant, and invoke cannot run, an action in ActionSpec::machine_forbidden; an eval gate with eval_id IS NOT NULL refuses a non-human or non-evals:approve decision and is never offered to a machine channel.
- AC-7 Config as data: no per-connector environment variable exists, and channels.get reports secret presence only, never a value.

## Verify commands

The recorded gate is the plan's §5 sequence at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix, whose affected binaries were re-run individually through the then-current rbuild test gate: `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-api --test channel_inbound`, `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-api --test channel_policy`, `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-server --test interaction_dispatch`, `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-api --test kata_role`, `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-api --test externals_declared` and `rbuild -- test -p conveyor-server --test prune`. The compile and lint verdict now comes from the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight workflow (`gh workflow run preflight.yml --ref <branch>`), never from a local compiling command.

## Results

At the recorded gate clippy and fmt were clean, the served OpenAPI lock passed, and every affected binary was green after the five-failure fix. The first full workspace run had found exactly those five failures and the rest of the suite passed. The full suite was not repeated end-to-end after the fixes, so AC-1 to AC-7 are evidenced by their named binaries, and a whole-workspace verdict is not claimed.

## Status

AC-1 to AC-7 are met at the recorded gate and carried by the suites named above; the plan's §5 result is the acceptance evidence. The one open status is the un-repeated full workspace run, recorded as S06d-I3 and closed only by a clean whole-workspace run on the pull request that lands this pack. No criterion is waived.

documents.title: Definition of Ready — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
documents.body:
# Definition of Ready — S06d Interaction Connector Standard

## Independent

S06d's build does not wait on an unmerged sibling slice: it consumes S02, S04, S05, S06, S06b and S06c, which the project row records as needs edges and which the 2026-11-28 snapshot shows measured built. The work lands in its own modules and its own test binaries, so a slice can be reviewed without another slice's branch in the diff.

## Negotiable

The standard's shape was negotiable while it was being written: which kinds ship first, which fields a ConnectorSpec carries, and how much of the command grammar is shared. The delivered cut is Telegram and the JSON webhook as the adapter kinds, with web as the human session and mcp as the licence principal, and the command vocabulary is the plan's §2 grammar rather than a fixed external contract.

## Valuable

The value is stated in the charter and the brief: the next interaction app is one registry entry instead of a new subsystem, config and credentials are rows instead of environment variables, and one approval resolves once across every channel with an auditable loss. Each benefit maps to a deliverable in the WBS rather than to an activity.

## Estimable

The plan enumerates the work in countable units: one migration (0038), four modules (channel, channel::command, channel::connectors, interaction), one inbound route, one worker hook for dispatch and close, and seven channels actions. The §5 gate names the binaries, so the size and the proof are both visible before the work starts.

## Small

The delivered scope fits one slice: the registry and its two adapters, the binding and grant tables, the inbound route, the shared grammar, the dispatcher and close sweep, and the policy actions. It adds no second state machine and no per-connector configuration surface, which is what keeps the change bounded to the connector seam.

## Testable

Every acceptance behaviour has a named suite: channel_inbound for the route and grammar, channel_policy for binding validation and the machine floor, interaction_dispatch for multicast and first response, and externals_declared for the absence of per-connector environment configuration. The plan's §5 gate is the single recorded verdict, so the Definition of Done can read one result per criterion.

## Dependencies

The typed dependencies are needs S02, S04, S05, S06, S06b and S06c, recorded on the project row in the 2026-11-28 snapshot. S02 supplies the workspace, tenancy and auth skeleton, S04 the registry and invoke authority, S05 projects and cards, S06 approvals and events, S06b the licence machine principal, and S06c the MCP task extension; S02, S04, S06b and S06c are closed and S05 and S06 are active while measured built.

# Definition of Done — S06d Interaction Connector Standard

## Acceptance criteria

One row per scenario in the acceptance-criteria document: AC-1 binding validation, AC-2 inbound interaction, AC-3 the shared grammar, AC-4 multicast, AC-5 first response, AC-6 the machine floor and eval refusal, and AC-7 config as data. At the recorded gate each row is met by its named suite, and the one row without a whole-workspace verdict is AC-7's externals check combined with the un-repeated full run, which stays open as S06d-I3.

## Evidence at completion

The completion evidence is the plan's §5 gate result at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix, `migrations/0038_s06d_connector_standard.sql`, and the suites `crates/api/tests/channel_inbound.rs`, `crates/api/tests/channel_policy.rs` and `apps/server/tests/interaction_dispatch.rs`. The pack's receipt is `docs/evidence/rework/S06d.json`, read against the seventeen checks in `acceptance/programme/S06d.toml` at the pinned snapshot.

## Repo gate

The repository gate at delivery time was the plan's §5 sequence: the workspace test suite, clippy with warnings denied, fmt check and the served OpenAPI lock. After the five-failure fix each affected binary was re-run individually and the lock passed. The current compile route is the GitHub-hosted preflight workflow; the pack adds the offline rework content check and the normal pull-request CI as its own gates.

## Merge and closure

The pack merges as the tranche-8 rework's content, and its closure is the record the close gate reads: charter, baseline statement, seven Phase A–D artefacts, five register kinds, delivery contract, WBS deliverable, Phase-G review, project brief, evidence output and closure review. risk.title: The close sweep's notification half can lose a closure notice
risk.body: The close action's status guard is the arbiter and the sweep is only the notification half. A worker stop between the guard and the sweep leaves the losing deliveries live until the next sweep, and the closure notice for that dispatch can be lost. The plan's trap 4 says a delivered sibling stays delivered and only live rows expire.
risk.response: Read the dispatch and delivery rows after a close in the interaction suite; if a live row survives a sweep, record the incident and repair the sweep, never weaken the status guard.

risk.title: A webhook sender can replay a command when a business refusal is read as a server failure
risk.body: Webhook senders retry non-2xx, so a business refusal must be a 200 ack and only a server-side failure may ask for a retry. A new connector that answers a refused command with a retryable status causes the sender to repeat it, and the dispatch primary key does not protect the inbound command path itself.
risk.response: State the refusal status in the connector contract and assert it in the inbound suite before a new kind is bound; treat a retried business refusal as a defect of the adapter, not of the sender.

risk.title: Migration 0038 lifts FORCE RLS on membership for the service-identity backfill
risk.body: The migration follows the 0028 pattern: it lifts FORCE row-level security on membership for the connector service-identity backfill and restores it before the migration ends. A failure inside that window would leave membership without forced row-level security, which is a tenancy exposure rather than a build problem.
risk.response: Keep the backfill inside one transaction and assert the restored FORCE flag in the migration's own verification; an operator re-reads `relrowsecurity`/`relforcerowsecurity` after any migration failure on membership.

issue.body: At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the project row records status closed and measured_status built while meta.closure_outputs is empty, and no closure review exists for S06d. The audit carries this as closed_without_closure_review:S06d. The capability and its suites exist; the closure record did not until this pack.

The build was gated; the lifecycle set around it was not authored at delivery time.

issue.title: The full workspace suite was not repeated end-to-end after the five-failure fix
issue.body: The slice plan's §5 records that the first full workspace run found exactly five failures, that each affected binary was re-run green after the fix, and that the full suite was not repeated end-to-end afterwards. A regression outside the affected binaries is therefore not excluded by the recorded gate, and no later record in this pack claims otherwise.

assumption.title: The tenant-admin grant matrix cannot widen the computed machine floor
assumption.body: machine_forbidden is computed from an action's declared scopes and resource, and both channels.policy_set and invoke enforce it. The assumption is that the computation is read at invocation time and has not been relaxed; if a stored grant could widen the floor, the standard's central security claim would fail.

dependency.title: S06d depends on S02, S04, S05, S06, S06b and S06c
dependency.body: The project row records needs edges to all six. S02 supplies the workspace, tenancy, auth, jobs and SSE skeleton, S04 the action registry and the invoke authority, S05 the project and card actions the grammar can reach, S06 the approval machine and events, S06b the licence machine principal that makes mcp a connector identity, and S06c the MCP task extension. At the 2026-11-28 snapshot S02, S04, S06b and S06c are closed; S05 and S06 remain active rows while measured built.

dependency.title: The standard is a prerequisite for every later interaction connector
dependency.body: Web, Telegram and MCP are the first three instances, and the standard exists so the next connector is one registry entry rather than a new subsystem. The project row records no outbound block on a named project, so this is carried as a dependency of the standard's consumers: a later connector that does not bind through the kinds registry and the shared grammar would reopen the cost S06d removed.

benefit.title: The next connector is one registry entry instead of a new subsystem
benefit.body: A ConnectorSpec per kind plus one binding row means the platform payload parser is the only per-kind code; the command grammar, identity, grants, retries and delivery state are core. The benefit is a structural reduction in the cost of adding an interaction app, declared in the charter and carried by the connectors module and the binding action rather than by a measured saving.

benefit.title: One approval resolves once across every channel, with the loss recorded
benefit.body: The dispatcher offers a pending approval to every eligible machine binding and human web inbox, and the first terminal decision expires the live siblings with a superseded last_error while sending one closure notice per dispatch. The benefit is a single decision with an auditable loss, and it is achieved without a second state machine.

benefit.title: The machine floor and human-only eval gates are enforced structurally
benefit.body: The machine floor is computed from declared scopes and resource and enforced at both policy_set and invoke, so no stored grant can widen it; the shared decision writer refuses a non-human or non-evals:approve decision on an eval approval, and the dispatcher never offers such a gate to a machine channel. The benefit is that the two boundaries hold without an operator remembering them.

project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

The connector standard is the built capability that makes a new user-interaction app one registry entry: a ConnectorSpec per kind carrying its typed config schema, secret names, default grants, capabilities and authenticate/parse/send functions; one binding row; one inbound route; one shared command grammar; one multicast dispatcher with a first-response close; and a tenant-admin grant matrix. Web, Telegram and MCP are the first three instances, and the next connector no longer rebuilds parsing, identity, grants, retries or delivery state.

## Boundary

S06d owns the connector registry, the binding and its config validation, the one inbound route, the command grammar, multicast dispatch, the first-response close and the policy matrix. It does not own the action registry or invoke (S04), projects and cards (S05), the approval state machine and events (S06), the machine principal (S06b) or MCP tasks (S06c). A second approval state machine, per-connector environment variables and machine grants for the web channel are explicitly outside it.

## Reuse sources

The slice plan's §2 table names what S06d reuses: the S06 approval state machine and its decision writer, the S04 action registry and Authority path, the S05 project and card actions reached through the grammar's do form, and S06b's licence principal for the mcp kind. Inside the crate the adapters reuse one config-schema validator, one sealed-secret accessor and one delivery-state writer rather than growing per-kind copies of each.

## Inception units

The plan's build order is the inception sequence: add migration 0038 with the binding, grant, dispatch and delivery tables under forced row-level security; define ConnectorSpec and the two shipped adapters; add the shared command grammar; add the one inbound route; add the multicast dispatcher and the close sweep to the worker; add channels.kinds/bind/get/list/unbind/test and channels.policy_get/set/reset; then regenerate the served lock. Each step names the suite the plan's §5 gate re-ran after the fix.

## Dependencies

The project row records needs edges to S02, S04, S05, S06, S06b and S06c. S02 supplies the workspace, tenancy, auth, jobs and SSE skeleton, S04 the registry and the invoke authority, S05 the project and card actions, S06 the approval machine and events, S06b the licence machine principal that makes mcp a connector identity, and S06c the MCP task extension. At the 2026-11-28 snapshot S02, S04, S06b and S06c are closed; S05 and S06 remain active rows while measured built.

## Acceptance

Acceptance is the slice plan's §5 gate at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix: clippy and fmt clean, the served OpenAPI lock OK, and the affected binaries re-run green — `conveyor-api --lib`, `externals_declared`, `kata_role`, `channel_inbound`, `channel_policy`, `conveyor-server --test prune`, `interaction_dispatch` and `conveyor-store --lib`. The full suite was not repeated end-to-end after the fixes, and this brief records that rather than implying a clean whole-workspace run.

## Capabilities

Connector onboarding as one registry entry; inbound interaction through one authenticated, parsed route; multicast approval delivery to every eligible channel; first-response resolution with the losing deliveries expired and one closure notice per dispatch; and tenant-admin governance through a stored grant matrix that can narrow but never widen the computed machine floor. Each capability is delivered by a named module in the Phase C catalog and exercised by a named suite.

## Plan

The plan is `docs/plans/slices/S06d-connector-standard.md`; the build is complete in the tree at the pinned snapshot, and this brief is the retrospective reading of it. The tranche-8 rework publishes the lifecycle set this brief belongs to, and the tranche-8 review is the forum that accepts the re-close. No further build step is claimed by this brief.

# Closure Review — S06d Interaction Connector Standard (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome vs acceptance

The standard's outcome is that the next interaction connector is one registry entry. Against the plan's §5 gate the recorded result covers clippy, fmt, the served lock and every affected binary at `99ed39f` plus the five-failure fix; the full workspace suite was not repeated end-to-end after the fixes, so that one limitation is carried as an open issue rather than folded into a pass. The retrospective level is compliant for the record set because the pack supplies the lifecycle and the receipt is green on every check the manifest can run.

## Evidence

The evidence is the slice plan and its §5 gate result, `migrations/0038_s06d_connector_standard.sql`, the suites `crates/api/tests/channel_inbound.rs`, `crates/api/tests/channel_policy.rs` and `apps/server/tests/interaction_dispatch.rs`, the receipt `docs/evidence/rework/S06d.json` at the pinned snapshot, and the seventeen checks in `acceptance/programme/S06d.toml`. The Phase-G review records the same set and names the packages it resolves.

## Open items

Three items stay open. The full workspace suite was not re-run end to end after the five-failure fix, and S06d-I3 carries that until a pull request runs it. The close sweep's notification half can lose a closure notice if the worker stops between the status guard and the sweep, which S06d-R1 records with a bounded impact. And a future connector kind can replay a command if it returns a retryable status for a business refusal, which S06d-R2 records against the webhook retry rule.

## Decision

The project is closed. The closure is taken by an approver other than the requester under the standing delegation, the closure review is recorded in the same pack, and the tranche-8 review is the forum that accepts it. No waiver is claimed, no check in the manifest is weakened to reach this decision, and the nine packages the review names are resolved by the artefacts, registers, contract and outputs this pack supplies.
